forecast-period.text: A low pressure system and associated trough over Western Australia move over western South Australia this evening and broadly across the state during Thursday, clearing to the east early Friday. A high pressure system will then move across southern SA from Friday, before a trough and cold front move across the west late Saturday and across the rest of SA on Sunday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and thunderstorms extending across most parts, clearing from the far west during the evening. Thunderstorms may tend severe over the Eyre Peninsula and the North West Pastoral district and its adjacent areas. Maximum temperatures near to below average in the far west but above average elsewhere. Northeast to northwesterly winds, freshening at times, ahead of a west to southwesterly change extending from the west, reaching Eyre Peninsula during the evening.

Showers and thunderstorms in the west, tracking into central parts overnight. Thunderstorms may be severe with heavy rainfall, damaging winds and large hail possible. North to northeasterly winds, fresh until later in the night. Winds tending east to southeasterly in the southeast.

Showers and isolated thunderstorms about central and eastern districts, clearing to the east by the evening. Maximum temperatures above average, tending near average in the west. North to northwesterly winds in the east ahead of a fresh west to southwesterly change. Winds tending southeasterly in the west from the evening.

Patchy morning fog about the Eyre Peninsula and Flinders Ranges. Light morning showers about southern coasts and the southeast. Showers and possible thunderstorms redeveloping about the agricultural areas late. Maximum temperatures above to well above average statewide. Light winds in the east tending north to northwesterly later. Freshening northeast to northwesterly winds in the west ahead of a west to southwesterly change in the far west later.

text.p: Isolated to scattered showers about the agricultural areas and adjacent parts to the north. Showers contract to the far northeast late, and linger about the southern agricultural area. Thunderstorms are possible about eastern districts during the day. Maximum temperatures above average, tending to below average in the far west. Freshening north to northwesterly winds in the east ahead of a fresh and gusty west to southwesterly change extending across during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Sunday: Generally, 2 to 10 mm across the state, with local falls of 10 to 20 mm possible about the southern agricultural area and in the far northeast. Falls of 10 to 20 mm west of about Coober Pedy to Ceduna are possible, with isolated falls of up to 30 m. Localised falls of 30 to 60 mm are possible with thunderstorms, particularly in the west - where higher falls are possible.
